subject.title: fix(plugin-sdk): guard assertHttpUrlTargetsPrivateNetwork against malformed URLs

question: Should the public plugin SDK intentionally standardize malformed URL failures as a sanitized `TypeError` preserving only the stable message and `ERR_INVALID_URL` classifier, while removing native parser fields such as `input` and `cause`?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but it deliberately changes the observable shape of errors from a public SDK function; repository policy treats that compatibility boundary as an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Approve sanitized contract
options.body: Accept the tested `TypeError` and `ERR_INVALID_URL` contract while intentionally excluding native fields that can retain sensitive endpoint input.

options.title: Define a named SDK error
options.body: Replace the ad hoc sanitized error with a documented exported error type if maintainers want a richer long-term public contract.

options.title: Keep native behavior
options.body: Decline the compatibility change and leave malformed URL handling to callers, accepting that the native error can retain rejected input.

recommendation.title: Approve sanitized contract
recommendation.body: Accept the tested `TypeError` and `ERR_INVALID_URL` contract while intentionally excluding native fields that can retain sensitive endpoint input.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent net-policy ownership work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the public SDK contract decision.
